title: Crashes and stuck programs
summary: Read a stack trace, and pause a program that never finishes.

say.never: When a program crashes, Java prints a **stack trace**. The first line says *what* went wrong. Each `at` line below it is a method that was running, starting with the one that crashed and going back to `main`. The number after the file name is the line. Click it to jump there.
say.bit: Line 1 is what went wrong; each `at` line is a method, crash first, with its line number.

board.code:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero
    at Pizza.slicesEach(Pizza.java:4)
    at Party.plan(Party.java:9)
    at Main.main(Main.java:3)

say.never: While the debugger is paused, the **Call Stack** section on the left shows the same list: which method called which to get here. Click any of them to see that method's variables at that moment.
say.bit: **Call Stack** shows who called whom; click one to see its variables.

board.code:
CALL STACK
  Pizza.slicesEach   Pizza.java:4
  Party.plan         Party.java:9
  Main.main          Main.java:3

say.never: It's tempting to wrap the crashing line in `try`/`catch` so the error goes away. That just hides it: the answer is still wrong, only quieter. Find *why* the bad value happened, and fix that.
say.bit: Don't hide a crash with try/catch; fix why the bad value happens.

say.never: A program stuck in a loop never crashes. It just never finishes. Start it with **Debug**, wait a second, then press **Pause** (‖) on the toolbar. The debugger stops wherever the program is *right now* and highlights the line. Step a few times and watch which variables change and which don't.
say.bit: A stuck program: Debug it, press **Pause** (‖), then step and watch what never changes.

steps.title: In your lesson: Read it from the top

say.never: `Main` crashes with `Index 3 out of bounds for length 3`, thrown in `Scoring.pointsFor`. `POINTS` has 3 boxes, numbered 0, 1 and 2, but levels are numbered 1, 2 and 3. So which box should level 1 use?
say.bit: `POINTS` has boxes 0-2, levels are 1-3. Which box is level 1?

say.never: Once the crash is fixed, `Main` gets stuck in `Cleaner.countValid`. Pause it, then step a few times. When `readings[i]` is below 0, `continue` jumps back to the top, and the `i++` at the bottom never runs.
say.bit: On a negative reading, `continue` skips `i++`, so `i` never moves.

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `Scoring`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name.
Your turn! Fix `pointsFor`, run `Main` again, then pause the stuck program and fix `countValid`. When it's all done, `Main` prints all seven lines.
